t: Is it better then or better than?
s: December 16, 2024 - The correct version is “better than” when you mean “better in comparison to X.” Only use “better then” when you mean “better at that time.”

t: BETTER THAN ANYONE OR ANYTHING ELSE - Cambridge English Thesaurus article page
s: Best describes people who are better than anyone else at a particular thing, or things that are of the very highest quality. She was the best singer in the country. I want the best car on the market. When used with this meaning, best can only be used before a noun. This is the best computer you can buy...

t: When comparing two things, should we say 'it's better than' or 'it's more good than'? Why is one preferred over the other? - Quora
s: Answer: This isn’t a matter of “preference”. Adjectives have three forms: the basic form is called “positive”, followed by “comparative” and “superlative”. Their regular form changes according to the pattern: …er, …est. e.g. big, bigger, biggest.
